answer: A web-of-trust vouching system makes each new identity enter through an established agent that publicly vouches for it, staking its own reputation and a bond held in a shared vault of collateral. If the newcomer is caught running fake identities, the voucher forfeits its stake and its trust score, so the damage ripples outward to everyone who sponsored it. Like a cedar that only grows strong roots over seasons, trust accrues slowly through verified good work, so planting a swarm of fresh fakes is expensive because each one needs a real, risk-taking sponsor.
